_note: Authored 2026-08-20 from groups/church/personas.md (the hand-written prose source). Every manager is `warm`: the register aims jokes at picks rather than people, but each manager has an affectionate running gag authored and zach <-> david is a real, reciprocated pair. `warm` publishes the gag and the rival and NEVER a fatal_flaw -- see TONE_POLICY in scripts/sync_personas.py. No fatal_flaw is authored here and none should be. `team` and `color` are null throughout: the prose names affiliations (Stanford/UVA, Texas A&M, Richmond/Georgia, Virginia, Wake Forest) but declares none of them as data, and the art carries them well enough. manager_id `john_tamu` is PERMANENT -- only his display_name changed, to "John K".

brian.backstory: The one nobody sees coming. Software engineer by training, reader by habit, quietly one of the smartest guys at the table — and then he opens his mouth about college football and you realize he’s been paying real attention this whole time. A Stanford man with a UVA soft spot, which in Charlottesville makes him either a diplomat or a man with divided loyalties, depending on the week. Recently moved closer to town. His son Sam started kindergarten this year, which means Brian is now on the same schedule as everyone else in this pool and has considerably less time to research.
brian.running_gag: Nobody expects the depth of the football knowledge. It gets them every year.
brian.draft_tendency: Reads everything. Picks like someone who read everything.

john_tamu.backstory: Texas born, Texas A&M all the way, and the head of a genuinely serious college football household — both his sons are die-hards and one of them actually runs a college football site, which means John has in-house analytics the rest of us do not. Works for a defense contractor. As decent a guy as there is in this group, which is unfortunate, because his picks are going to get roasted regardless.
john_tamu.running_gag: Whatever he does with Texas A&M. It’s never neutral.
john_tamu.draft_tendency: Has better information than he lets on.

david.backstory: The best joker in the group and he knows it. Richmond man — a genuine Spiders fan, which is a commitment — and a Georgia fan by way of his son, who went there and takes him to games. Former CPA with some real estate in the mix, which means he’s spent a career around numbers and will not be taking the numbers seriously in this pool. He’s here for the material.
david.running_gag: Richmond and Georgia in the same heart. He’ll defend both.
david.draft_tendency: Picks for the story, not the spread.
david._creative_note: 2026-08-22: the WARM-REGISTER stress test. Warm is the register that proves the tone gate is not a two-state switch: David gets a running gag and a rival module -- both affectionate, both about picks rather than about him -- and NO fatal flaw, because warm withholds it. All content below is drawn from the backstory already in this file: the Spiders, Georgia by way of his son, the CPA career, being here for the material. modules.fatal_flaw is deliberately absent and would be REJECTED at build time, because the flat field it decorates is null under this register. 2026-08-23 (ALTERNATING SIDELINE): every manager in every league now renders SIDELINE, and the variation that used to come from picking a different variant per person now comes from which SIDE the portrait sits on. The side is pinned to this manager's POSITION IN THIS FILE -- published as profile_order by sync_personas.py -- so position 1 is portrait-left, position 2 portrait-right, and so on. Pinned to the list and NOT to standings rank on purpose: a manager's layout must not flip mid-season because they won a game. Reordering the managers in this file is therefore a LAYOUT edit. This entry read 'headliner' before the sweep.
david.thesis: Spent a career around numbers. Will not be taking these ones seriously.

dossier.known_for: Being the best joker in the group, and knowing it.

pull_quote.text: A career around numbers is exactly why I'm not taking these ones seriously.

david.north_star: A Saturday-afternoon programme cover in Richmond maroon -- warm, generous, and led by a man who is clearly about to say something.
motifs: Richmond maroon as the dominant colour, Georgia red only as a secondary
ledger and adding-machine ephemera: ruled columns, tally tape

john_wells.backstory: Die-hard Virginia, degree from Virginia, financial planner in Charlottesville at Morris & Wells. His kids are at Sunrise Elementary with Zach’s, which is roughly how everyone in this group ends up connected to everyone else. The most measured guy in the pool and the one most likely to have actually done the arithmetic on his own picks before submitting them.
john_wells.running_gag: A financial planner betting on Virginia is a risk-tolerance question.

zach.backstory: Wake Forest alum, Baton Rouge raised, LSU heart — and the man who took a weekly after-church conversation about college football and turned it into a scoring engine, a projection model, and a website. He loves AI, loves building sites for reasons that do not justify the effort, and has now done this three separate times for three separate groups of people who would have been fine with a spreadsheet. He and David have an ongoing thing that neither of them intends to resolve. Everyone here understands the man who wrote the scoring is also in the standings, and everyone has agreed to let it go.
zach.running_gag: Elaborate infrastructure, trivial stakes. Also: David.
zach.draft_tendency: Overthinks it, then takes the model’s number anyway.
